title: The Law of Implicit Dependencies
hook: You fixed a tiny bug and a customer got upset because they'd been relying on it.
statement: Once enough people use your product, someone depends on every little thing it does, even the accidents.
explainer: It doesn't matter what you documented or promised. With enough customers, someone builds around every quirk. Change anything they can see and you'll break something for somebody.
sop: List everything users can see your product do, not just what's documented.
Separate what you mean to guarantee from what's accidental.
Calculate Breakage Risk from Users × Exposed Surface.
Hide internals so users can see less.
Announce and phase out changes before you make them.
equation_example: 10,000 Users × 50 visible behaviors = 500,000 spots where someone might depend on you. Higher means any change is more likely to break someone. Shrinking either number lowers the risk.
question: Write down one quirk in your product or process that customers have started relying on.
closing_statement: Be careful what you show people. They'll build on it.
caption:
Principle Nº 357: The Law of Implicit Dependencies

You fixed a tiny bug and a customer got upset because they'd been relying on it.

Once enough people use your product, someone depends on every little thing it does, even the accidents.

Your turn: Write down one quirk in your product or process that customers have started relying on.
